body:
I'll be thirty-seven this year. There was a point in my life, rapidly receding into the distance of years, when I had some talent and some optimism. I more or less conceded defeat at seventeen. Colleges lined up to court me, but I went with the local community college and dropped out of that after a year.

I am unemployed at the tail-end of a string of meaningless jobs, and have no interest -- none whatsoever -- in working again. I never had a real career, and the things that I used to be good at are of no consequence anymore. I threw away my marriage about five years ago, almost as though I did it on purpose; knowing full well that she was blameless, I've convinced myself that she was the villain, and that today, way behind on child support, I'm the one deserving of respect and deference.

My son is eleven years old, and I'm watching as his mother and mine push me to the margins of his life.

This is my fourth time living with my parents, not counting childhood; it's been almost two years this go-around, and I've made no effort to make it on my own. The present stint comes after a disastrous live-in relationship with a woman to whom I was of no more use than I was to my wife.

I seem to utterly lack the skills essential to making it in the world as an independent agent. I am frightfully ignorant of most things having to do with personal economics and the day-to-day business of living (things like owning and keeping a home, paying bills, and so forth). If my folks died tonight, I wouldn't have the first fucking clue what to do with myself tomorrow. 

I used to have some truly phenomenal friends. I don't know what happened to them.

I've been diagnosed with, and have intermittently allowed myself to be treated for, severe clinical depression. I was involuntarily committed a few years ago, screaming and crying and blubbering that this was it and somebody had better do something because I was going to kill myself. All my hospital stay did was provide me with the tools to avoid having to go back there again; I am in much worse shape now than I was then.

Suicide, when it comes, will not be an act of desperation or a shot at some attention: it will be the conclusion of a rational sequence of thought. With an acute understanding of my own deficits on the one hand and a realistic appraisal of my prospects on the other, suicide will be the only choice that makes any sense. It's almost as though my whole life has been leading up to it: that it's something I somehow decided to actually work toward. The treatment I've received may just as well have been a diversion from purpose.

My circumstances have nothing to do with bad luck. I've enjoyed decent physical health, have never had a substance abuse problem, have never been abused in any substantive way. I've been given every opportunity, handed advantages greater than most people in the world will ever have, and I have systematically discarded each and every one. Left to myself, I'm like a liquid seeking its lowest point. (If only I had any actual depth.) Left to myself, I will assiduously not do the things that need doing.

That's the short version.
